newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ANGRY COLE DISMISSES RUDDOCK'S EXPLANATION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ANGRY COLE DISMISSES RUDDOCK'S EXPLANATION.

text.p: An angry Andy Cole criticised Neil Ruddock on Tuesday after a challenge by the Liverpool defender left the Manchester United striker with two broken legs.
Ruddock's tackle in Saturday's reserve game at Anfield between Liverpool and Manchester United, left the United striker sidelined until the New Year at least.

Ruddock, who is expected to replace the injured Dominic Matteo when United host Liverpool in the premier league this Saturday, insists there was no malice in his challenge and that he asked Cole if he was all right.
But Cole disagrees with Ruddock's version of events.

"I am disappointed in what he has said that there was no ill feeling and that he came up to me when I was on the ground," said Cole. "He didn't. I have had no contact with Neil Ruddock at all. He never said anything to me after the game, nothing whatsoever.
"His opinion is that he didn't mean to do it but if he didn't mean to do it then why make those kind of challenges?
"If those challenges come in every game then people are going to get seriously hurt."
Ruddock was reported as saying: "There was certainly no malice in my challenge. I thought I had a chance of getting the ball so I slid in."
An X-ray on Cole revealed that the cracked bone in one leg may have been an old injury although his ankle in the other is broken in two places.

But United's record signing, who cost Alex Ferguson 6.0 million pounds ($9.37 million) plus Keith Gillespie when he moved from Newcastle in 1995, has vowed to bounce back from his latest setback and prove himself at Old Trafford.
"I may not play again until the New Year but I will come back even better and prove that I am good enough to play for Manchester United," he claimed.

"When I came back from the pneumonia I had this summer I felt stronger and I thought that I was doing well and getting my fitness back. Now I think that I will come back stronger from this minor setback."
